lead.hed: USNI: Destroyer Chafee refueled the Seahawk unmanned vessel at sea
lead.insight: USNI News, Tuesday: USS Chafee (DDG-90) conducted an at-sea fueling of Seahawk, a Medium Displacement unmanned surface vessel, on Sept. 11 in the Pacific. The Navy announced the evolution Monday as part of its work on at-sea drone sustainment. The official still shows Seahawk alongside Chafee during that fueling. Practice evolution, not a combat employment.
lead.image_credit: U.S. Navy photo by Lt. j.g. Charles Winkowski · DVIDS 9955366 · Public domain · USV Seahawk fueling alongside USS Chafee (DDG 90), Sept. 11, 2026.

political.hed: Defense News: Royal Navy launched a U.S. Mk 48 from the Excalibur unmanned sub
political.insight: Defense News, Tuesday: the Royal Navy launched a U.S. Navy Mk 48 heavyweight torpedo from the British Excalibur uncrewed underwater vehicle on Sept. 13 at the British Underwater Test and Evaluation Centre in Scotland. Adm. Daryl Caudle, chief of naval operations, called it a first for allied undersea interchangeability under AUKUS Pillar 2. Proof of concept, not a deployed weapon.

political.hed: Defense News: F-16 crashes at Spangdahlem; pilot ejected and is in treatment
political.insight: Defense News, Tuesday: an F-16 assigned to Spangdahlem Air Base in western Germany crashed Tuesday. The U.S. military said one pilot ejected safely and was receiving medical treatment, and that the cause is under investigation. German air traffic control said four F-16s were in a training exercise; one is believed to have crashed on approach, and the others landed at Ramstein.

political.hed: Heritage: China is moving toward a new form of coercion at sea
political.insight: Heritage Foundation, Tuesday: since Beijing announced special maritime operations on June 6, Chinese forces have pushed patrols into new waters, rotated formations to regularize presence, and deployed research vessels that can conduct military reconnaissance. Commentary on that pattern, not a U.S. statute.

tech.hed: Defense News: CENTCOM has become a battle lab for unmanned systems
tech.insight: Defense News, Tuesday: unmanned systems have moved from exercises into an active war. After a U.S. Army helicopter went down near the Strait of Hormuz in June, a Navy unmanned vessel helped recover two service members. A month later, CENTCOM said three Corsair sea drones struck a submarine and ship maintenance facility at Bandar Abbas — the first time American forces employed sea drones in combat. Field use, not a procurement decision.

tech.hed: USNI: Britain posts its 2026 nuclear enterprise update to Parliament
tech.insight: USNI News, Tuesday: the U.K. Defense Nuclear Enterprise 2026 Annual Update to Parliament, released Sept. 15, says the deterrent delivered by the Royal Navy through Operation Relentless since 1969 remains at the heart of British national security. Document post, not a new treaty.

culture.hed: WORLD: Heart of the Beast keeps the combat dog alive, then gets dark
culture.insight: WORLD, Tuesday: a review of David Ayer’s Heart of the Beast, rated PG-13 and in theaters. Brad Pitt plays a retired Green Beret stranded in Alaska with his former combat dog. The reviewer says the opening shot establishes that the dog survives, and that the survival film is not all sunshine. Film review, not a policy fight.

culture.hed: Law & Liberty: Tomkins asks whether courts or elected government decide policy
culture.insight: Law & Liberty, Tuesday: Adam Tomkins reviews the question of which disputes belong in court and which belong to elected government. He notes that, in the United States, abortion, the death penalty, and same-sex marriage became matters of legal right rather than legislative policy. Book review, not a statute.
